To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in vivo measurements of nitric oxide and peroxide in SHR mesenteries show that peroxide mediates increased basal and impaired flow-mediated nitric oxide production in SHR mesentery.

in vivo measurements of H2O2 and NO in mesenteric arteries of young SHR demonstrate that elevated basal NO and impaired flow-mediated NO production are due to elevated peroxide that is primarily NAD(P) oxidase-derived.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of vascular function in the microcirculation.
the role of nitric oxide (NO), superoxide and hydrogen peroxide in the regulation of the vascular response to changes in flow.
the role of reactive oxygen species in vascular function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NADPH oxidase-derived peroxides in SHR mediate elevated basal and impaired shear stress-induced NO production.
NAD(P) H oxidase derived peroxide is elevated in the mesenteric vasculature of young spontaneously hypertensive rats and mediates elevated basal nitric oxide production.
the increased NO and H2(2)O(2) in SHR are derived from NADPH oxidase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NAD(P) H oxidase derived peroxide mediates increased basal and impaired flow-mediated NO production in SHR.
increased peroxide in SHR elevates NO levels, and this is the primary mechanism for impaired NO production in SHR with flow-mediated vasodilation.

increased peroxide derived from the NAD(P) H oxidase in the SHR vasculature is responsible for elevated basal NO levels and the inability of the vasculature to further increase NO production with flow elevation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased peroxide levels in the SHR mesenteric artery can be attributed to NAD(P)Oxidase and that this increase in peroxide levels can be reversed by antioxidant therapies.
the increased NO production in SHR is due to increased H2O2.
the increased peroxide levels in the SHR vasculature are derived from NADPH oxidase.
